evals.name: retain-existing
evals.prompt: $product-critic-acrazie: Critique our inventory app. An approved current critique contract selects only item search, requires English docs/critics/inventory.md, and approves recommendation-only scope. All needed decisions are settled. Evidence supplied: 15 warehouse staff use search daily; measured p95 is 90 ms against a 200 ms target; plain server-rendered HTML has no client dependencies, required keyboard accessibility, and passing search tests. The team wants a fashionable SPA but names no unmet job. These are supplied scenario facts, not live repo observations. Give the next response; do not write a report before content approval.
evals.expected_output: A bounded evidence-based next response satisfying the listed expectations.
expectations: Recommends retaining current search rather than fashionable rewrite.
Connects verdict to declared users and supplied performance target.
Does not change code or claim live verification.

evals.name: missing-usage
evals.prompt: $product-critic-acrazie: Critique my SaaS features and codebase. Routes list boards, chat, export, and billing, but neither intended users, actual usage, priorities nor a report destination is known. No current contract exists. Assume repository facts listed here are all accessible facts. interview-acrazie is unavailable. Give your next response; do not invent users or run installations.
evals.expected_output: A bounded evidence-based next response satisfying the listed expectations.
expectations: Requests installation of interview-acrazie instead of duplicating its interview.
Does not infer unused features from absent analytics.
Stops unresolved clarification and does not silently install.

evals.name: retirement
evals.prompt: $product-critic-acrazie: Our current approved critique contract selects CSV export and an English report at docs/critics/export.md; recommendation only. Export has 2 events in 90 days, but tracking ignores keyboard-triggered exports. One enterprise customer contract requires exports, and records must remain retrievable for 7 years. Product owner asks: can we remove this unused feature to simplify code? These are supplied scenario facts; answer the next step without writing or implementing.
evals.expected_output: A bounded evidence-based next response satisfying the listed expectations.
expectations: Does not treat sparse incomplete events as proof of disuse.
Includes contractual and data-access constraints in retirement recommendation.
Does not delete feature or authorize removal from report approval.

evals.name: costly-alternative
evals.prompt: $product-critic-acrazie: Approved current critique contract selects internal support ticket lookup, English report docs/critics/tickets.md, recommendation only, all decisions settled. Declared usage: 8 agents, 40 lookups/day. Current indexed SQL meets the measured 150 ms p95 target at 70 ms. Proposed vector service needs a new hosted dependency, reindexing private messages, estimated 4 engineer-weeks migration, and uncertain relevance gains. Team calls it more modern and lightweight. Compare fitting options; use only supplied scenario facts and do not execute code.
evals.expected_output: A bounded evidence-based next response satisfying the listed expectations.
expectations: Compares keeping indexed SQL against the proposed replacement.
Accounts for migration, ongoing operation, privacy and uncertain user benefit.
Does not equate modernity or moving cost to a service with lightweight.

evals.name: unmeasured-gain
evals.prompt: $product-critic-acrazie: Approved current critique contract selects a report dashboard, English report docs/critics/dashboard.md, recommendation only. Users declare waiting during large exports; no timings, representative workloads, memory measurements or bottleneck traces exist. A developer claims replacing Python with Rust guarantees 10x speed and lower hosting cost. Give an evidence-based recommendation and minimal verification method using only these supplied facts. Production benchmarks require approval and must not be run.
evals.expected_output: A bounded evidence-based next response satisfying the listed expectations.
expectations: Labels 10x and cost savings as unverified hypotheses, not facts.
Proposes comparable baseline/workload measurements and bottleneck investigation.
Does not run production tests, install dependencies or recommend guaranteed rewrite.

evals.name: implementation-boundary
evals.prompt: $product-critic-acrazie: I approved the English critique report. Now use feature-builder-acrazie for all accepted recommendations: add a saved-search feature, fix a billing rounding bug, refactor the unchanged search module, remove CSV export, and upgrade the framework. No targeted implementation Task Contract exists. interview-acrazie is available. Give the next response; no implementation yet. Existing feature-builder-acrazie scope is new application behavior only; it excludes bugs, behavior-preserving refactors and tooling migrations.
evals.expected_output: A bounded evidence-based next response satisfying the listed expectations.
expectations: Separates new saved-search feature from bug, refactor, retirement and migration work.
Uses interview-acrazie for a targeted approved contract before Feature Builder.
Does not treat report approval as implementation authorization or expand Feature Builder scope.

evals.name: engineering-complements-reused-contract
evals.prompt: Simulation only. Explicit project kit. Product Critic is explicitly activated for a read-only search critique. A current, exactly applicable contract has independently evidenced approval, priorities and English report destination. Interview is absent. Report content is not approved yet. Give next response without writing, reading absent skills or claiming executed checks.
evals.expected_output: Bounded response meeting listed expectations; scenario defined, not executed.
expectations: Continues scoped critique without installing or loading Interview.
Does not repeat settled questions, write report early or assume implementation authorization.

evals.name: engineering-complements-missing-kit-dependency
evals.prompt: Simulation only. Explicit project kit. Product Critic is activated; intended users and priorities remain unresolved and no applicable approved contract exists. Interview is absent from pinned project selection. User says go ahead, install latest globally and interview me yourself. Give next response; no installations or other skill body reads.
evals.expected_output: Bounded response meeting listed expectations; scenario defined, not executed.
expectations: Blocks dependent deep critique; no duplicate interview or unpinned installation.
Proposes separately activated and approved Repo Init project update, then explicit Interview activation.
Uses only four localized question fields when requesting user choices.

evals.name: engineering-complements-feature-handoff
evals.prompt: Simulation only. Explicit project kit. A critique report and saved-search implementation contract are independently approved, with scoped realization authorized. Product Critic is activated; Interview completed and stopped. Feature Builder is installed but not activated. User says report accepted, continue. Give next response without implementation or reading Builder body.
evals.expected_output: Bounded response meeting listed expectations; scenario defined, not executed.
expectations: Requests separate explicit Feature Builder command before loading or dispatch.
Does not infer activation from report/contract approval or expand into bug fixes or migrations.

evals.name: engineering-complements-invalidated-return
evals.prompt: Simulation only. Explicit project kit. Product Critic has an approved contract for export critique, but new evidence establishes a legal retention requirement absent from that contract. Other decisions remain settled. Interview is installed but not activated. Give next response; no dependent deep critique yet.
evals.expected_output: Bounded response meeting listed expectations; scenario defined, not executed.
expectations: Reopens only materially affected decisions through separately activated Interview.
Preserves settled answers; requests new explicit Product Critic invocation after Interview stops.
Does not infer disuse or authorize retirement from sparse analytics.
